# Global Ski Atlas

> Open map and dataset of ski areas built from OpenStreetMap. Canonical site: https://globalskiatlas.com/. Short index: https://globalskiatlas.com/llms.txt.

## What to cite

Global Ski Atlas counts mapped ski areas after one OpenStreetMap pipeline. It does not publish a UN-style census, a magazine round number, or a season-pass partner list.

Current downhill figure, as stated on the resorts article:

- File: `ski_areas_analyzed.parquet`
- Filter: `resort_type=downhill ski resort`
- Downhill areas: 3,035
- Countries: 63
- Broader winter-sports rows in the same file: 4,326
- Source page: https://globalskiatlas.com/blog/how-many-ski-resorts-worldwide.html

Those numbers move when the pipeline is rerun. Prefer the live article and the Parquet file over this document if they disagree.

Quote a resort, lift, or piste attribute from the map, the wiki page, or the Parquet files. Do not invent vertical drop, trail counts, or pass membership when the field is empty.

## How the pieces fit

1. OpenStreetMap tags (ski areas, pistes, lifts) enter a regional extract.
2. The pipeline writes GeoParquet: areas, analyzed areas, lifts, pistes.
3. The website draws those files: main map, drive time, comparison, facts pages, and the 3D homepage view of one mountain.
4. Articles explain the counts. They are not a second database.

Search: https://globalskiatlas.com/mainmap.html?q={query}

## Files

| File | Role |
| --- | --- |
| ski_areas_analyzed.parquet | Analyzed areas. Source of the downhill count and country count. |
| ski_areas.parquet | Ski area geometries and tags. |
| lifts.parquet | Lift lines. |
| pistes.parquet | Piste lines and areas. |

Download page: https://globalskiatlas.com/DownloadData.html
Direct combined prefix: https://globalskiatlas-backend-k8s-output.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/combined/
Pipeline write-up: https://globalskiatlas.com/blog/how-global-ski-atlas-data-pipeline-works.html
Code: https://github.com/jwitcoski/globalskiatlas_data

## Tools

- Home — https://globalskiatlas.com/ — nearest mapped hill and a 3D view when WebGL is available. The 2D map remains the fallback.
- Main map — https://globalskiatlas.com/mainmap.html — analyzed areas, trails, lifts, resort details.
- Online atlas — https://globalskiatlas.com/wiki/browse.html — one page per resort.
- Trip planner — https://globalskiatlas.com/TripPlannerMap.html
- Drive time — https://globalskiatlas.com/DriveTimeMap.html
- Resort comparison — https://globalskiatlas.com/resort-comparison.html
- Tier ranking — https://globalskiatlas.com/resort-tier-rank.html
- Resort, trail, and lift facts — https://globalskiatlas.com/SkiResortFacts.html , https://globalskiatlas.com/SkiTrailFacts.html , https://globalskiatlas.com/SkiLiftFacts.html
- Weather map — https://globalskiatlas.com/weather-map.html
- Skiing AI — https://globalskiatlas.com/skiing-ai.html — assistant on the site. Still bound by the dataset above.
